## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Vitakka Sutta* ("Thoughts", Iti 38; It 2.11, PTS It 31) is a discourse found in the *Itivuttaka* of the Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. The text sets forth two distinct thoughts that habitually arise in the Buddha as he dwells delighting in non-ill will and seclusion [SuttaCentral].
Textual parallels and shared passages are widely attested across early Buddhist literature in Pali, Sanskrit, Tibetan, and Chinese [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. Curated passage-level parallels identified by SuttaCentral include narrative contexts in the *Mahākhandhaka* of the Vinaya (Kd 1), the *Mahāpadāna Sutta* (DN 14), the *Pāsarāsi Sutta* (MN 26), the *Bodhirājakumāra Sutta* (MN 85), and the *Brahmāyācanasutta* (SN 6.1) [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral also identifies parallels in the Sanskrit *Mahāvadānasūtra* (SF 36), the Sanskrit, Tibetan, and Chinese recensions of the *Udānavarga* (UV 21, UVS 21, Uv Kg 21, D4099, T 212, T 213), and a resembling Chinese parallel in T 765.88 [SuttaCentral]. The sutta is additionally cited in exegetical canonical texts, including the *Tuvaṭakasuttaniddesa* (Mnd 14), *Sāriputtasuttaniddesa* (Mnd 16), and *Mogharājamāṇavapucchāniddesa* (Cnd 19) [SuttaCentral].
In agreement with these curated parallels, DharmaNexus detects significant Pali-internal text reuse, particularly in segment ranges §7.5–8.6, shared with Kd 1, SN 6, DN 14, MN 26, MN 85, the *Buddhavaṃsa-aṭṭhakathā*, and the Niddesa treatises [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also aligns the text cross-linguistically with the Sanskrit *Mahāvadānasūtra*, the Sanskrit and Tibetan *Udānavarga*, and the Chinese *Madhyama Āgama* (T 26) [DharmaNexus].
No secondary literature in the reference dossier directly discusses Iti 38; matching search results under the title *Vitakka Sutta* discuss the *Dvedhāvitakka Sutta* (MN 19), while citations referencing "It. 38" cite page 38 of the Pali Text Society edition of the Itivuttaka (which contains Iti 44).
*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
